title: Give the business rule business values
intro: The eligibility calculation can run without an HTTP request, database row or RAP message object.
context: Method body of your own policy class. amount and minimum are importing decfloat34 values; blocked is an importing abap_bool; result is the returning abap_bool. The caller supplies values and translates the result into its UI or service response.
code:
METHOD is_eligible.
  result = xsdbool(
    amount >= minimum
    AND blocked = abap_false ).
ENDMETHOD.

highlights.label: Calculate one business decision
highlights.explanation: The method compares the amount and blocked flag. It does not read an HTTP request, issue SQL or build a framework message.

highlights.label: Return a simple result
highlights.explanation: The caller receives abap_true or abap_false. A RAP adapter can report the decision without making the policy class depend on RAP response types.

outcome: For amount 500, minimum 300 and blocked = abap_false, the result is true. A unit test can check that rule without an HTTP server or a database.
caveat: A deliberately small policy, not a complete approval process or authorization check. Keep permission checks, currency rules, meaningful rejection reasons and transaction ownership in the complete design. No SAP execution is claimed.

references.title: SAP Clean ABAP: methods and testability

title: The wrapper still calls a dependency
intro: Renaming a call or converting its result does not change the release status of the API behind it.
context: Method body of a custom wrapper in a classic component on a system that permits this design. dependency is a bound object with a declared read_order method; order_id and result use your custom public types. Assume the implementation behind dependency was checked and still uses an unreleased SAP object. No particular SAP API is invented here.
code:
METHOD read_order.
  DATA(ls_order) = dependency->read_order(
    order_id = order_id ).
  result = CORRESPONDING #( ls_order ).
ENDMETHOD.

highlights.label: Follow the actual call
highlights.explanation: This is the next dependency to inspect. Releasing the custom wrapper for its callers does not release the SAP object used underneath.

highlights.label: Separate mapping from classification
highlights.explanation: Mapping into your own result type can protect callers from some interface changes. It cannot remove the implementation's original dependency or upgrade risk.

outcome: The caller sees a small custom interface, but the dependency still needs its real classification, an owner, tests and a replacement plan. The whole chain has not become Level A.
caveat: Illustrative wrapper body with prerequisite types and methods, not a workaround for restricted ABAP Cloud or Public Edition. Inspect actual SAP calls and configured implementations; this fragment alone cannot establish a Clean Core level.

references.title: SAP Learning: Clean Core checks and release contracts
